evidence.quote: It's not just the money, it's being in the club and it's the signalling that we're in the game.
evidence.speaker: Dr David Blaney

evidence.quote: The Sêr Cymru initiative has been quite important in doing that, because it's been very focused, capturing key research players, and the attractiveness that that has then to other researchers around them, and to industry collaboration, and they have been areas of real strength that we've invested in.
evidence.speaker: Dr David Blaney

evidence.quote: And I think they are already showing dividends in terms of the capacity to win more research funding, and to establish an even stronger presence in the international research market.

evidence.quote: Okay. Just one further point, from Darren.

evidence.quote: Just very briefly, one of the pieces of feedback that the committee members received at a stakeholder engagement event, which took place prior to this inquiry starting, to receive oral evidence, was about the research funding that is available from the charitable sector, and how poorly Wales does in attracting some of that research.

evidence.quote: I appreciate that research into the type of activity that they want to put their money into, Wales may not be particularly good at, and there may be other opportunities with other charities and partnerships.

evidence.quote: One of the issues is the capacity to engage with that funding, because of the overhead issue that David mentioned.

evidence.quote: There is an element in England.

evidence.quote: But that pressure's the same in other parts of the UK, is it not? So the overhead funding is still an issue in England, and in other places.

evidence.quote: So, the more you're able to invest—.
